subject: Novum MSA — trademarked output & model-training carveouts
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, legal@novum.com
Cc: patentcounsel@brandtlaw.com, ops@novum.com
Date: 2028-06-13T09:12:00Z
Subject: Novum MSA — trademarked output & model-training carveouts

Hi all,

Attaching Novum's latest MSA redline and our working notes (Novum_MSA_redlines_20280611.pdf, Trademark_List.csv). Two narrow but important asks from Novum that we need to resolve before the final order form:

1) Customer ownership of "Trademarked Output" — customer wants explicit title over any generated outputs that include their trademarks or product names and to prohibit use of those outputs for model training.
2) Broad training prohibition — they want a blanket restriction on using any customer-related outputs for model training or quality improvements unless they opt in.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Customer retains title to Customer Content and to any Output that contains Customer Trademarks (we can call this "Trademarked Output").
- Redwood retains a narrow, non-exclusive feedback license to use non-identifying output and telemetry for service improvement and bug fixes.
- Explicit carveout: Redwood will NOT use Trademarked Output to train foundation models or to include in publicly shared datasets. Usage for delivery, debugging, or anonymized aggregate telemetry is permitted.

Questions for legal: can we land on language that prevents training on trademarked output while preserving the operational telemetry we depend on (e.g., token-level failure signals, crash logs)? If we need to define an "anonymization standard" (hashing + truncation + minimal context), please propose a short clause.

Priyom — commercial: if we accept the trademark carveout, we should offer a managed telemetry package (higher tier) where Novum can opt-in to broader telemetry sharing for a fee. Thoughts?

Laura — can you sanity-check the proposed scope from an ops/assurance perspective and list anything that would break our SLOs?

Novum legal — can you confirm whether your concern is limited to trademarked product names/branding or if it extends to any output that references Novum internal product identifiers?

Next steps: I suggest we agree core language today and produce a one-page summary to send back.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-06-13T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Novum MSA — trademarked output & model-training carveouts

Vivek / team,

Quick thoughts:
- The trademark carveout sounds reasonable but we need a durable definition for "Trademarked Output." Recommend: any generated output that contains an exact match to a string in the submitted Trademark_List.csv or content that Novum reasonably identifies as brand proprietary within 7 days of delivery.
- For telemetry: we cannot rely on raw full-output logging for continuous model improvements where Novum is concerned. Suggest we accept hashed/hashed-sample telemetry (SHA256 token-level hashes with context window of +/- 5 tokens) plus error counters.
- Operational impact: the main risk is if debugging requires reproducing a full exchange; we should retain the ability to capture a transient, encrypted snapshot for 48 hours accessible only to on-call staff and scrubbed if flagged by Novum.

If legal is happy with the above, I'll draft a short clause to add to the MSA (3-4 lines) and a fallback process for incident debugging.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-06-13T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Novum MSA — trademarked output & model-training carveouts

Vivek / counsel,

Quick note from trademark perspective. Draft clause below (redline attached):

"Trademarked Output and Customer Trademarks. Customer retains title to any Output that reproduces or materially incorporates Customer Trademarks or Customer-specific trade dress ("Trademarked Output"). Redwood shall not use Trademarked Output or Customer Trademarks for model training, derivative model creation, or inclusion in datasets used for training without Customer's prior written consent. Redwood may use Trademarked Output for the sole purposes of (i) delivering the Service, (ii) resolving incidents and debugging, and (iii) short-term, pseudonymized quality monitoring, provided that such data is retained no longer than forty-eight (48) hours, is secured per the parties' SLA, and is not used to train any general-purpose model."

Suggested edits: add an explicit timeframe for retention (48 hours), define permitted operational uses, and exclude aggregated telemetry from the prohibition provided individual identifiers are removed.

See attached mark-up: BrandtLaw_MSA_trademark_redline.pdf

Regards,
A. Brandt
Senior Counsel, Brandt Law

Subject: Re: Novum MSA — trademarked output & model-training carveouts

Thanks — this is heading in the right direction. Couple commercial points to call out before legal locks language: 

- We should offer Novum two options: (A) Standard Tier: accepts trademark carveout as drafted (no training on Trademarked Output; hashed telemetry only) — no price change; (B) Telemetry Opt-in: allows Redwood to use de-identified, longer-retention telemetry and limited model-tuning for product improvements for a defined fee (suggest +12% of ARR or a per-token uplift). This gives Novum flexibility and preserves our upgrade path.
- Escrow/incident path: if Novum wants us to reproduce a specific user conversation for bug triage and that conversation contains Trademarked Output, require a short written consent (DocuSign) to lift the restriction for that record only — auto-sunset after 48 hours. I'll prepare a one-click DocuSign flow.

If legal approves operational wording, I'll send the choice matrix to Novum and propose a call tomorrow to finalize.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Novum MSA — trademarked output & model-training carveouts

Team / Novum,

Thanks for the quick turn. Summary of agreed points we can put in the redline:

1) Definition: "Trademarked Output" = any generated Output that exactly matches or materially incorporates items from customer's provided Trademark_List.csv, plus any content customer reasonably designates within 7 days.
2) Prohibition: Redwood will not use Trademarked Output or Customer Trademarks to train foundation models, produce derivative models, or include in public datasets without prior written consent.
3) Permitted operational uses: Delivery of service, incident reproduction (with short written consent per-record), on-call debugging snapshots retained up to 48 hours, and aggregated anonymized telemetry for quality monitoring.
4) Optional commercial path: Telemetry Opt-in for extended retention and limited tuning scoped and priced separately (we'll include an option in the order form).
5) Evidence & audit: Redwood will maintain an access log for any temporary reproductions and provide Novum with a report on retention events quarterly (redacted).

Action items:
- Laura: please incorporate the Brandt Law language into the MSA redline and add the hashed-telemetry standard (Laura will attach redline).
- Priyom: draft the Opt-in pricing language and DocuSign flow.
- Legal (Novum): once we receive the updated redline, please confirm whether the Trademark_List.csv is the authoritative list for auto-classification or if you want to reserve the right to flag additional items.

If there's no material pushback, I'll have Marissa circulate the final redline and a 1-page summary for Novum's GC to sign by Friday.

Best,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
